papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and machine learning to develop a prognostic signature based on tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The signature identifies potential therapeutic targets and links TDT to molecular heterogeneity and immune microenvironment features, offering a new tool for patient stratification.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This study benchmarks bioinformatics tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with long-read Nanopore sequencing, which can capture full-length transcripts and better resolve alternative splicing. The authors generated paired short-read and long-read datasets to systematically compare the performance of different computational methods. The findings provide guidance on tool selection for researchers working with long-read single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of an antibody dependent cellular phagocytosis related signature for hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The reduced phagocytic activity of macrophages in the tumor microenvironment (TME) and the presence of anti-phagocytic factors in cancer cells hinder the effectiveness of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in clinical settings. Consequently, our objective was to create a risk assessment model using antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP) regulators to serve as prognostic indicators and immunotherapy markers for individuals with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
papers.summary: This study developed a risk assessment model based on antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP) regulators to predict prognosis and immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Using multi-omics data, the authors identified an ADCP-related signature that could serve as a prognostic indicator and help guide immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment decisions.

papers.title: Single-cell mitophagy patterns dictate intercellular crosstalk in the tumor microenvironment to promote osteosarcoma progression.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is a highly aggressive primary bone malignancy in adolescents, with poor prognosis due to limited diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of cancer, and mitophagy, the selective clearance of damaged mitochondria, critically maintains cellular homeostasis. However, the specific role of mitophagy in shaping the OS tumor microenvironment (TME) at single-cell resolution remains poorly understood. This study aims to systematically characterize mitophagy patterns within the OS TME and investigate their impact on intercellular communication, tu
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell analysis to characterize mitophagy patterns in osteosarcoma, revealing how mitochondrial clearance in tumor cells influences intercellular communication within the tumor microenvironment to drive cancer progression. The findings provide new insights into the role of mitophagy in shaping the tumor ecosystem and suggest potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A Simple, Cost-Effective, High-Throughput Method for Measuring Chromatin Accessibility and Gene Expression in Single Nuclei.
papers.abstract: We describe microfluidic-free, droplet-based methods for single-nucleus epigenomic measurements: Particle-templated Instant Partition single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (PIP-ATAC-seq) and its multiomic version (PIP-Multiome-seq). We benchmarked these assays by generating data sets containing thousands of nuclei using cell lines and mouse brains and compared to other established methods. PIP-Multiome and PIP-ATAC are straightforward to implement, affordable, and produce high-quality data, providing useful additions to the single-cell molecular measurement
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces PIP-ATAC-seq and PIP-Multiome-seq, microfluidic-free, droplet-based methods for measuring chromatin accessibility and gene expression in single nuclei. These assays are cost-effective, easy to implement, and produce high-quality data comparable to established methods, making them valuable tools for single-cell epigenomic research.

papers.title: CAdir: Joint clustering of cells and genes for single-cell transcriptomics with visualization-driven cluster quality assessment.
papers.abstract: Clustering for single-cell RNA-seq aims at finding similar cells and grouping them into biologically meaningful clusters. Many available clustering algorithms however do not not provide the cluster defining marker genes or are unable to infer the number of clusters in an unsupervised manner as well as lack tools to easily determine the quality of the label assignments. Therefore, clustering quality is commonly evaluated by visually inspecting low-dimensional embeddings as produced by, e.g., UMAP or t-SNE. These embeddings can, however, distort the true cluster structure and are known to produc
papers.summary: CAdir is a new method for single-cell RNA-seq clustering that simultaneously clusters cells and identifies marker genes, and includes a visualization-driven tool to assess cluster quality without relying on potentially misleading UMAP or t-SNE embeddings. This addresses key limitations of existing algorithms by providing unsupervised cluster number inference and integrated marker gene detection.

papers.title: CellCover defines marker gene panels capturing developmental progression in neocortical neural stem cell identity.
papers.abstract: Defining cell classes is central to the analysis of growing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlases. Marker genes are most often identified by differential expression (DE) methods that assess genes one at a time, ignoring the redundancy and complementarity revealed when genes are considered jointly. Working with binarized expression data, we instead seek discriminating panels of genes that together are specific to a cell type, framing marker-panel selection as a variant of the minimal set-covering problem in combinatorial optimization. This formulation efficiently searches the vast spac
papers.summary: CellCover is a new computational method that selects minimal sets of marker genes to define cell types from single-cell RNA-seq data, treating the problem as a combinatorial optimization task rather than using traditional differential expression. Applied to neocortical neural stem cells, it identifies gene panels that capture developmental progression more effectively than standard approaches.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial transcriptomics can be applied to study cancer epigenetics, highlighting that traditional sequencing methods lose spatial context by disrupting tissue architecture. The authors argue that spatial biology approaches are crucial for understanding how local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs influence tumor development and heterogeneity.

papers.title: A Unified Developmental Timeline of Pigmented Ocular Tissues in the Mouse Eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: This study presents a unified developmental timeline of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye using a gentle bleaching method that preserves immunohistochemical markers, overcoming the traditional challenge of melanin interference. By combining this approach with re-analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data, the authors provide a comprehensive atlas of coordinated development across pigmented ocular structures.

papers.title: Decoding neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts unveils a shared target reservoir for immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Primary liver cancer, predominantly hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), has limited therapeutic options. While mutation-derived neoantigen vaccine holds promise, its success is hindered by low antigen availability. This study explores transcriptome-derived neoantigens (neoantigen-encoding tumor-specific transcripts, neoTSTs) in HCC, characterizing their features, generation mechanisms, and therapeutic potential.
papers.summary: This study identifies a new class of neoantigens derived from tumor-specific transcripts (neoTSTs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), which are more abundant than mutation-derived neoantigens and may serve as shared targets for immunotherapy. The findings suggest that neoTSTs could overcome the limitation of low antigen availability in HCC, offering a promising avenue for vaccine development.

papers.title: Autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus: insights from integrative multi-omics analyses.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by the emergence of autoantibodies and deposition of immune complexes. SLE presents with heterogeneous multi-organ involvement that varies among patients and its mechanisms have been investigated to facilitate appropriate stratification and treatment selection. Bulk RNA-seq and bulk ATAC-seq have provided important insights into the pathogenesis of SLE; however, these approaches are inherently limited by their reliance on predefined cell subsets and known markers, which can introduce bias and restrict their ability to fu
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrative multi-omics analyses, including bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, have advanced understanding of autoreactive B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), an autoimmune disease with heterogeneous organ involvement. It highlights the limitations of these bulk approaches due to reliance on predefined cell markers and suggests that newer single-cell technologies may overcome these biases to improve patient stratification and treatment selection.

papers.title: Robust and generalizable CNV detection for single-cell sequencing assays.
papers.abstract: Copy number variations (CNVs) are genomic structural variants that are strongly linked to cancer progression and genetic disorders. CNVs can be highly heterogeneous at population and tissue scale; thus, single-cell resolution detection holds great promise for studying clonal evolution and CNV-driven changes. Despite advanced sc-RNA-seq CNV detection methods, accurate methods for epigenomic single-cell modalities lag behind. We developed RIDDLER; a robust, unsupervised method that uses outlier-aware statistical modeling to detect CNVs across multiple single-cell modalities and assays. RIDDLER u
papers.summary: This paper introduces RIDDLER, a new computational method that uses outlier-aware statistical modeling to detect copy number variations (CNVs) from single-cell sequencing data. Unlike existing methods that are limited to RNA-seq, RIDDLER works robustly across multiple single-cell modalities including epigenomic assays, enabling more comprehensive study of CNV heterogeneity in cancer and genetic disorders.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses a single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) to identify a key antagonistic relationship between the epigenetic modifiers Nsd1 and Ezh2 in mouse embryonic stem cells. The authors show that Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 opposes Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 to orchestrate the transition between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal mechanistic insights of FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most prevalent and aggressive subtype of renal malignancy, characterized by extensive vascularization and poor prognosis. Early detection markedly improves patient outcomes, and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA, encoded by FOLH1) imaging has recently emerged as a valuable diagnostic tool for ccRCC. However, the cellular source, spatial distribution, and mechanistic contribution of FOLH1 expression within the tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial multi-omics to identify FOLH1+ endothelial cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and reveals their potential role in tumor vascularization and progression. The findings provide mechanistic insights into how these cells may contribute to the tumor microenvironment and could inform future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Scalable hypothalamic neuron differentiation from human pluripotent stem cells suitable for modeling metabolic disorders.
papers.abstract: The hypothalamus, composed of multiple nuclei, is essential for maintaining the body's homeostasis. Within the mediobasal hypothalamus, the arcuate nucleus (ARC) contains key neuronal populations, including appetite-suppressing pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons that regulate energy and glucose balance. Here, we present a chemically defined, scalable method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) into hypothalamic neurons enriched for POMC cells, compatible with robotic cell culture platforms for high-throughput use. Neuronal identity was validated by MERFISH single-cell tran
papers.summary: This paper presents a new, scalable method for differentiating human pluripotent stem cells into hypothalamic neurons, specifically those that produce POMC, which are key regulators of appetite and metabolism. The method is chemically defined and compatible with robotic platforms, enabling high-throughput studies of metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Identification of potential diagnostic biomarkers for myocardial infarction using bioinformatics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction(AMI)is an important type of cardiovascular disease, which seriously threatens the lives of humans. In order to help patients receive timely clinical treatment and improve their survival rates, it is necessary to screen out related molecules in advance. To this end, we applied bioinformatics methods and machine learning algorithms to find possible biomarkers associated with AMI. When considering possible connections with dynamics of immune cells activation. Based on the RNA-seq results, differential expression analysis was performed followed by WGCNA to identify stab
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics and machine learning to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), with a focus on immune cell dynamics. The authors performed differential expression analysis and WGCNA on RNA-seq data to find molecules that could enable earlier diagnosis and improve patient survival.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics identifies CYP1B1 as a candidate molecular link between toxicant exposure and ferroptosis-related epithelial stress in COPD.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by progressive airflow limitation, chronic airway inflammation, and epithelial remodeling. Although oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation are increasingly recognized as important contributors to COPD pathobiology, the epithelial biomarkers and regulatory pathways linking cigarette-smoke exposure to ferroptosis-related injury remain incompletely defined.
papers.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative multi-omics approach to identify CYP1B1 as a potential molecular link between cigarette smoke exposure and ferroptosis-related epithelial stress in COPD. The findings suggest that CYP1B1 may serve as a biomarker and therapeutic target for COPD by connecting toxicant exposure to oxidative damage and lipid peroxidation.

papers.title: PathwayBench: a multi-criterion benchmark of pseudobulk pathway activity scoring methods reveals rank-window competition as a mechanism of biological signal loss in single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: Pathway activity scoring is a foundational step in single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analysis, yet method choice is rarely guided by systematic, multi-criterion evidence in the pseudobulk case-control regime that now dominates applied single-cell disease studies. Prior single-cell pathway-scoring benchmarks have focused on perturbation ground truth at cell-level resolution, leaving the donor-level pseudobulk setting - and the question of why methods disagree - largely unaddressed.
papers.summary: This study introduces PathwayBench, a multi-criterion benchmark for evaluating pseudobulk pathway activity scoring methods in single-cell RNA-seq case-control studies. The authors find that method disagreement arises from 'rank-window competition,' a mechanism where biological signal is lost when genes with similar expression ranks compete for limited pathway representation, leading to systematic biases in pathway activity estimates.

papers.title: PLNFGL: joint estimation of multi-condition gene networks from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Graphical models have been widely used in bioinformatics to infer the conditional dependence structure among random variables, but traditional Gaussian graphical models (GGMs) are suboptimal for single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) due to dropout events and distributional mismatch. Moreover, most existing methods estimate networks under a single condition, limiting their utility in multi-condition studies.
papers.summary: This paper presents PLNFGL, a new method for jointly estimating gene regulatory networks across multiple conditions from single-cell RNA-seq data, addressing issues like dropout events and distributional mismatches that plague traditional Gaussian graphical models. By leveraging information across conditions, it improves network inference accuracy and enables comparative analysis of network rewiring.

papers.title: Identifying condition-related cell-cell communication events using supervised tensor analysis.
papers.abstract: Many tools have been developed to infer active cell-cell communication (CCC) events, which are essential for understanding biological processes and diseases. However, existing methods for assessing the relationships between CCC events and biological conditions have at least one practical limitation: a lack of clear interpretation, an inability to adjust for confounders, or an inability to model inherent dependencies among CCC events. To comprehensively address these limitations, we introduce STACCato, a supervised tensor analysis tool for identifying condition-related CCC events. STACCato empl
papers.summary: This paper introduces STACCato, a new supervised tensor analysis tool that identifies cell-cell communication events related to specific biological conditions while overcoming limitations of existing methods, such as lack of interpretability and inability to adjust for confounders. The tool models dependencies among communication events, offering a more robust approach for studying disease-related cellular interactions.

papers.title: A pan-cancer single-cell atlas uncovers the role of sex hormones and chromosomes in sex-divergent reprogramming of the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Sex bias is pervasive in tumors; however, how sex chromosomes and hormone-responsive signaling shape the tumor microenvironment (TME) remains insufficiently characterized. Considering the critical impact of the TME on tumor progression and response to immunotherapy, a pan-cancer investigation of sex-specific and cancer-context-dependent TME features is warranted.
papers.summary: This study uses a pan-cancer single-cell atlas to investigate how sex hormones and chromosomes contribute to differences in the tumor microenvironment between males and females. The findings reveal sex-divergent reprogramming of the TME, which may influence tumor progression and immunotherapy responses.

papers.title: PRECISE: A Prognostic Thyrocyte-Derived Gene Signature for Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) exhibits heterogeneous behavior, underscoring the need for effective biomarkers and improved risk stratification methods. We developed a thyrocyte-derived gene signature, Prognostic RNA Expression Cell-specific Integrated Signature (PRECISE), using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) and evaluated its prognostic utility across cohorts.
papers.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
papers.summary: Researchers developed a new gene signature called PRECISE from single-cell RNA sequencing data to better predict outcomes in papillary thyroid carcinoma. This signature, derived specifically from thyrocyte cells, improved risk stratification across multiple patient cohorts compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Discovery of hub genes linking oxidative stress to type 2 diabetic sarcopenia using single-cell sequencing and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and sarcopenia demonstrate a significant comorbidity, particularly in the elderly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking them, especially through oxidative stress, remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes involved in T2DM-associated sarcopenia (T2DS) by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk RNA-seq data with machine learning. We analyzed scRNA-seq datasets (GSE244515, GSE268953) to characterize cellular heterogeneity and bulk RNA-seq datasets (GSE202295, GSE226151) for differential expre
papers.summary: This study identifies key oxidative stress-related genes linking type 2 diabetes and sarcopenia by combining single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with machine learning. The findings may help uncover molecular mechanisms underlying this comorbidity in the elderly.
